questions.question: Which language should the browser workbench use?
questions.rationale: A typed frontend suits a workflow-oriented workbench and supports predictable UI state.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed language for the browser application.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should the workbench use?
questions.rationale: React is a practical default for a structured multi-stage workbench.

options.label: React
options.description: Component-based browser UI; pairs with Fluent UI v9.

options.label: Vue
options.description: Component-based browser UI; pairs with Vuetify 3.

options.label: Svelte
options.description: Compiler-based browser UI; pairs with Skeleton UI.

options.label: Angular
options.description: Full-featured application framework; pairs with Angular Material.

options.label: Plain HTML
options.description: Minimal browser UI; pairs with Pico.css.

questions.question: What should the first release include? Confirm or edit this scope.
questions.answer: Guidance workbench with real workflow actions and agent-style support panels; AEP, BizApps Platform, and agent-service steps are manual and explicitly trackable, with no live integrations in the first release.
questions.rationale: The repository provides lifecycle guidance but no AEP, BizApps Platform, or agent API endpoints.
questions.recommendedChoice: Guidance workbench with real workflow actions and agent-style support panels; AEP, BizApps Platform, and agent-service steps are manual and explicitly trackable, with no live integrations in the first release.

questions.question: What approved Avanade brand assets or visual rules should be used? If none are available, confirm a text-only brand treatment without invented logos or colors.
questions.answer: Use Avanade name text only with a restrained brand-inspired palette; do not use logo assets or invent trademark artwork.
questions.rationale: No approved brand assets or verifiable brand specifications are present in the repository.
questions.recommendedChoice: Use Avanade name text only with a restrained brand-inspired palette; do not use logo assets or invent trademark artwork.

questions.question: Which data stores does the first release need?
questions.rationale: A browser-only first release can present the existing guide without persisting project records.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use repository guidance and browser-local state only; no shared persistence.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Shared relational persistence for project workbench state.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Shared relational persistence for project workbench state.

questions.question: Will users sign in to use application API features in the first release?
questions.rationale: The proposed first release has no backend API; live enterprise integrations would require revisiting this choice.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users sign in to access application API features.

options.label: No
options.description: No sign-in for application API features in the first release.
